# PHASE-004 - Implement explicit migration

| Field | Value |

| Depends on | PHASE-003 |

## Objective

Provide exact, fail-closed, stale-protected v1-to-v2 migration with truthful atomic receipts.

## Scope

- Migration command
- Legacy evidence preflight
- State and body conversion
- Atomic publication and recovery

## Entry conditions

- PHASE-003 read-only mixed-catalog behavior is stable.

## Exit criteria

- All legacy state mappings and placeholder conversions work.
- Meaningful legacy evidence blocks before mutation.
- Failure and partial-publication paths are recoverable without blind retry.

## Risks

- Migration is the highest data-integrity risk.
- Per-record commits require exact partial-sequence reporting.

### Risks

- A broad or implicit migration route could rewrite unintended records.

### Acceptance criteria

- Migration targets exactly one resolved record per invocation.
- Missing confirmation, stale digest, ambiguous selector, lock, unsafe path, or unsupported schema returns without mutation.
- The receipt distinguishes canonical commit and index publication.

### Planned verification

- Run exact ID, filename, and full-title migration selection cases.
- Run ambiguity, stale, no-confirmation, and unsafe-path negatives.

### Risks

- False negatives could discard historical evidence; false positives could block safe placeholder migration.

### Acceptance criteria

- Unchecked boxes and known empty evidence markers qualify as placeholders.
- Checked boxes and meaningful Evidence or Completion evidence produce exact field-level blockers.
- Preflight performs no canonical or index write.

### Planned verification

- Test every documented empty marker and several meaningful evidence strings.
- Compare full filesystem snapshots after blocked preflight.

## TASK-016 - Publish migration atomically

Integrate stale rechecks, catalog and record locking, private temporary writes, atomic canonical replacement, index publication, partial receipts, and bounded recovery for migration.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | `completed` |
| State reason | None |
| Skip authority | None |
| Requirements | REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-013, REQ-014 |
| Design basis | None |
| Target artifacts | SKILLS-depo/to-trd/scripts/trd.py |
| Dependencies | TASK-015 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | 2026-09-04T21:22:05.471667Z |

### Risks

- A canonical commit followed by index failure could be misreported or blindly retried.

### Acceptance criteria

- Pre-commit failures leave canonical and index bytes unchanged.
- Canonical success plus index failure returns a truthful partial result and exact reindex route.
- Owned temporary and lock cleanup follows existing safety boundaries.

### Planned verification

- Inject canonical replacement and index publication failures.
- Verify stale state before and after lock acquisition.
- Run the documented recovery route without repeating migration.
